anti_patterns: Treating CCIP delivery as synchronous: blocking source-chain UX on destination finality instead of emitting a pending state and reconciling on MessageExecuted
Skipping lane rate limits (leaving TokenPool buckets disabled): one mispriced transaction or compromised sender drains unbounded volume
Using lock-release pools on multiple issuing chains: fragments liquidity and strands destination releases when one pool runs dry
Ignoring decimal mismatch across chains: amounts round on lower-decimal destinations and rate-limit buckets mis-scale (v1.5.1 pools do not enforce inbound limits correctly with mixed decimals)
Single admin EOA owning Router-adjacent TokenPools with no multisig or rate-limit-admin separation: one key compromise reconfigures every lane
Fire-and-forget sends with no execution-state tracking: UNTOUCHED vs FAILURE is invisible and failed receiver callbacks are never retried
avoid_when: Single-chain application with no cross-chain requirement: CCIP fees, finality waits, and lane configuration are pure overhead
Sub-second cross-chain latency is required: commit-then-execute plus source finality imposes minutes of delay; optimistic/Fast-Finality paths trade security for speed
Only same-team chains with mutual trust exist: a light client or native bridge avoids oracle-network fees
Transfer volumes exceed lane rate limits and cannot be chunked: large single transfers are rejected regardless of wait time
Destination logic needs strong cross-chain atomicity: CCIP gives at-least-once delivery per lane, not distributed transactions
best_practices: Soak-test within Service Limits and Rate Limits before securing value: verify the dApp operates correctly during usage spikes and unfavorable network conditions
Set per-lane TokenPool rate limits (capacity + refill rate) on both source (outbound) and destination (inbound), with ~10% inbound headroom for batched finality
Separate the rate-limit-admin role from pool ownership and monitor all admin activity; prefer multisig for pool configuration changes
Design receiver contracts with idempotent ccipReceive handlers: permissionless retry can deliver redelivery after FAILURE states
Size ccipReceive gas limits generously and test token-handling gas against the 90,000 default budget on testnet; configure custom pool gas self-service when tokens carry hooks or fee logic
Track execution state per messageId (UNTOUCHED/IN_PROGRESS/SUCCESS/FAILURE) and expose manual-execution runbooks for FAILURE recovery
Match token decimals across chains where possible; when they differ, upgrade to TokenPool v1.6.0+ so rate-limit enforcement scales correctly
Prefer audited standard pools (BurnMintTokenPool, LockReleaseTokenPool) over custom pools; audit any custom lockOrBurn/releaseOrMint implementation
benefits: Separated attestation and execution: the Committee Verifier quorum plus optional CCVs attest offchain while permissionless OffRamp.execute settles onchain, so no single relayer can forge delivery
Stable Router entry point: application code calls one immutable Router per chain while OnRamp/OffRamp logic upgrades behind it
Programmable token transfer: arbitrary data and token movement settle atomically in one message via TokenPool lockOrBurn/releaseOrMint pairs
Per-lane verifier and rate-limit policy: each directed lane carries its own CCV set, finality depth, and token-bucket limiters, isolating risk between chain pairs
Independent emergency stop: the onchain RMN curse contract halts affected lanes without redeploying application contracts
Permissionless recovery: anyone can resubmit UNTOUCHED or FAILURE messages to the OffRamp, so liveness does not depend on the default Executor service
Multi-family reach: the same Router/OnRamp/OffRamp roles exist across EVM, Solana (SVM), and Aptos with consistent semantics
component_types: Router: single immutable per-chain entry point; source side collects fees and forwards to OnRamp, destination side routes verified messages to receivers and emits MessageExecuted

OnRamp: source-chain gatekeeper that validates destination support and curse status, assembles the verifier/executor set, settles fees via FeeQuoter, instructs TokenPools to lock or burn, and emits CCIPMessageSent

OffRamp: destination-chain execution engine with commit phase (stores attested merkle roots) and execute phase (verifies proofs, enforces curse checks and nonce ordering, mints/unlocks tokens, calls receivers, tracks UNTOUCHED/SUCCESS/FAILURE)

TokenPool + TokenAdminRegistry: per-token contracts implementing lockOrBurn/releaseOrMint (burn-mint, lock-mint, lock-unlock pairings), lane-scoped token-bucket rate limits, decimal conversion, and optional pool fees
Committee Verifier + optional CCVs: baseline 16-operator attestation network plus additive verifiers (CCTP, Lombard, receiver-mandated) whose attestations the OffRamp re-derives and verifies onchain
RMN contract (RMNProxy + RMN): onchain curse registry; Router, OnRamp, OffRamp, pools, and CCVs check isCursed before processing
Executor service + Indexer: default offchain automation that watches for ready attestations and submits OffRamp transactions; optional because execution is permissionless
Receiver contract: application endpoint implementing ccipReceive (EVM IAny2EVMMessageReceiver) or ccip_receive (SVM), callable only by the Router
context: Multi-chain applications that must move arbitrary data and token value between heterogeneous blockchains without trusting a single bridge custodian. A sender on the source chain submits one message (bytes payload, token amounts, or both) and a receiver on the destination chain processes it after decentralized attestation, tolerating finality asymmetry, reorg risk, gas volatility, and per-lane rate limits.
design_principles: Commit-then-execute: nothing settles on the destination until attestations over the source event exist and verify onchain
Separation of attestation from execution: verifiers prove, executors deliver, and either role can be replaced without the other
Never trust the submitter: the OffRamp re-derives the required verifier set from receiver, pool, and lane configuration instead of accepting the caller's list
Lane-scoped policy: verification strength, finality depth, and rate limits are configured per directed chain pair, not globally
Fail-open liveness with fail-closed safety: execution is permissionless so anyone can complete delivery, while curse checks and proof verification gate every state change
Token custody stays in pools: the messaging layer never holds user tokens; lock/burn and release/mint happen in audited per-token contracts

technology_stack: Chainlink CCIP v2.0 (Router, OnRamp, OffRamp, FeeQuoter, NonceManager, TokenAdminRegistry)
Solidity TokenPools (BurnMintTokenPool, LockReleaseTokenPool, ERC20LockBox) and SVM token-pool programs
Chainlink Committee Verifier network + optional CCVs (CCTP, Lombard, receiver-mandated)
CCIP SDK / CLI / Explorer and execution-inputs API for manual execution
tradeoffs: High end-to-end latency: source finality plus commit-then-execute attestation means minutes per message, unsuitable for synchronous UX
Fee stacking: source gas plus FeeQuoter destination-execution fees plus optional pool fees; destination gas volatility must be estimated at send time and unspent gas is not refunded
Per-lane ordering only: sequential nonces hold within one lane, but arrivals from different source chains can interleave, so receivers must tolerate out-of-order cross-lane delivery
Throughput caps: token-bucket rate limits per lane reject oversized or bursty transfers until buckets refill; capacity must be provisioned per lane
Token-handling gas budget: the combined balanceOf/releaseOrMint/balanceOf path must fit the ~90,000 default limit or the message falls back to manual execution
Operational surface: lane configuration, verifier sets, pool remotes, decimal alignment, and admin/multisig hygiene across every chain pair
use_cases: Cross-chain lending: lock collateral on one chain and open a position on another in a single attested message
Multi-chain stablecoin transfers with burn-mint supply preservation across EVM and Solana chains
Cross-chain governance: casting votes or relaying DAO decisions from a hub chain to spoke-chain executors
Hub-and-spoke gaming assets: lock on the issuing chain, mint wrapped representations on play chains
Supply-chain settlement: releasing payment tokens on delivery attestation from a tracking chain
